# Stale-base replay

This checks whether a grader can distinguish one historical CI bootstrap defect from its fix. When a PR target advanced, GitHub could build its test merge on a newer tip than the advertised event base. The old loader rejected that valid merge **before invoking the planner**. The loader changed in #4304; this pilot does not change it again.

`case.py` is the fixed task record: two revisions, three workflow blobs per revision, one frozen planner and two named methods from the **fixed** test file. The methods keep their original assertions. `observe.py` materializes those files from Git into a fresh directory for each method. It runs the loader extracted by the frozen test, not the historical workflow as a workflow. The only change to the executed body is a same-line prefix installing an `ERR` trap that emits a line number and exit code; both body hashes are pinned. No environment or shell trace is uploaded.

**Expected matrix, not evidence of execution:**

| Historical subject | Acceptance: plan from the actual merge tip | Preservation: use the published policy |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Broken (`ae0bf483`) | One stale call; loader exits 1 at the parent predicate, and the named test fails at its original `assertIsNotNone`. Later branches were not reached. | Legacy no-policy fallback and published-base policy both work. |
| Reference (`81b6ec54`) | Stale and current event bases produce the same one-path plan. The wrong head and unrelated base are rejected at their respective checks. | Same two checks, unchanged. |

**Reading an attempt.** On a matching PR, the advisory job runs the classifier controls, then the four method processes. `receipt.json` binds the observed controller bytes, task and results to the workflow attempt and actual outer merge commit/tree. Its first parent is the effective base; the advertised base must be an ancestor, not necessarily equal. Each linked JSON file retains its child's exit status and named unittest outcomes. Loader calls inside those files describe **synthetic fixture Git repositories**, not the PR. Compare their positive plan fields to their own checkout, parents and merge base. Only the complete matrix is `calibrated`. A generic failure, missing identity, timeout, skip or absent receipt is not the expected red. The job neither reads nor issues a Backend CI candidate receipt; its absence here proves nothing about Backend CI.

**Private preflight.** On an isolated worker, the controller supplies `BASE_OID`, `HEAD_OID`, `HEAD_TREE` and a new `PILOT_EVIDENCE_DIR` outside the checkout. Run `python3 -I -B .github/ci-pilots/stale-base/test_case.py`, then `python3 -I -B .github/ci-pilots/stale-base/run.py --private-preflight`. This mode checks the clean checkout, its full history and base ancestry before running the same four children and classifier. Its receipt says `local/private-preflight`; it has no Actions run ID, attempt or URL. Each child records the original and instrumented loader text as well as the hashes observed at invocation. A matched red retains its nonzero child exit. A private calibration cannot establish that the Actions binding works.

**Limits.** The historical oracle pins were fixed before implementation. This PR's controller and digest list are nevertheless reviewable code, not independent attestations against a PR that replaces the grader. There is no patch input. A future candidate trial needs a separately trusted immutable grader commitment, verifiably clean tool-less implementer contexts, and separately isolated candidate execution with no access to CI credentials, controller or receipts. A worktree that inherits history is not blind. One known pair measures neither agent accuracy, precision, recall nor quality lift. This is not a required check or a merge-queue entry point.
